findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket (including the seeded vendor roster spreadsheet) are not covered by an enforced SSE-KMS default encryption policy.

No ACL is declared and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so there is no guardrail preventing a later ACL or bucket policy from granting public read/write to report data.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial ledger data stored without an enforced encryption default or customer-managed key control.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a subsequent bucket policy or object ACL from exposing financial exports publicly.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without enforced server-side encryption defaults.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket, leaving it exposed to accidental public access via a future ACL or policy change.

The runbooks bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block; runbooks commonly contain internal hostnames, procedures and occasionally credentials, and are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the runbooks bucket, so nothing prevents a future policy or ACL from publishing internal operational documentation.

findings.issue_category: invalid canned ACL on log bucket
findings.description: The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid canned ACL (it appears to be a corrupted "log-delivery-write"), so the intended log-delivery grant is not applied and the audit destination bucket's access control is not what was intended.
The central audit log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so no guardrail prevents a policy or ACL from exposing accumulated audit logs publicly.
force_destroy = true on the central audit/log-delivery bucket allows the bucket and all accumulated audit logs to be deleted in a single apply, enabling anti-forensic destruction of the audit trail.
The bucket that receives access logs for model_artifacts has no logging configuration of its own, so tampering with or reading the audit trail itself is not recorded.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that has no default encryption configuration, so potentially sensitive third-party data is stored without KMS protection.
